name: Prof. Mahadev Satyanarayanan (Satya)
position: Carnegie Group University Professor of Computer Science
research_summary: The widely recognized founding father of Edge Computing / Cloudlets. Pioneer of the Coda File System and Andrew File System (AFS). Directs the Living Edge Lab at CMU.
edge_relevance: Defined the foundational concept of Cloudlets in 2009, creating the entire modern discipline of Edge Computing.
research_trajectory: From distributed storage systems (AFS, Coda) to mobile client-server computing, cloudlets, cyber foraging, and wearable cognitive assistance.

recruitment.evidence_text: Accepts PhD students through CMU Computer Science Department admissions; actively mentoring researchers on edge systems and cognitive assistance.

potential_phd_topics: Next-Generation Cloudlet Synthesis for Ultra-Low Latency Wearable Cognitive Assistance
Privacy-Preserving Edge Video Streaming Under Variable Cellular Bandwidth
Bandwidth-Efficient Distributed State Synchronization Across Mobile Edge Enclaves
why_suitable: Original pioneer and father of Edge Computing (Cloudlets) in world computer science history (ACM/IEEE Fellow)
Direct leadership of CMU's Living Edge Lab with world-class industrial partnerships and testbeds
Full 5-year guaranteed doctoral fellowship funding at Carnegie Mellon University
Unmatched prestige, mentorship quality, and alumni placement in academic and industrial leadership
research_gaps: Sub-10ms end-to-end latency preservation when synthesizing full VM container state on remote edge cloudlets
Mitigating client thermal throttling during sustained on-device preprocessing before cloudlet transmission

publications.title: The Emergence of Edge Computing
publications.research_problem: Centralized clouds cannot satisfy latency, bandwidth, and survivability needs of mobile devices.
publications.approach: Decentralizing compute into proximal two-tier cloudlet architectures.
publications.key_contribution: Foundational canonical paper defining edge computing across industry and academia.
publications.edge_relevance: The seminal foundation of the entire discipline.

publications.title: Offload Shaping for Wearable Cognitive Assistance
publications.research_problem: Cloudlets are far less elastic than cloud data centres, which limits how well low-latency edge-offload applications scale.
publications.approach: Offload shaping on wearable devices (mapping processes to tiers, gating and decluttering), evaluated with four wearable cognitive assistance applications on three devices.
publications.key_contribution: Large reductions in network use and cloudlet load compared with sending full camera frames, without losing accuracy or performance.
publications.edge_relevance: Context-Aware Activity Recognition Systems (Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition)

name: Prof. Ion Stoica
department: Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Sciences (EECS)
position: Professor of Computer Science & Co-Director of Sky Computing Lab
research_summary: World-renowned computer systems pioneer (co-creator of Apache Spark, Ray, Chord DHT, and co-founder of Databricks and Anyscale). Co-directs the Sky Computing Lab at UC Berkeley.
edge_relevance: Pioneers Ray and Sky Computing frameworks enabling seamless distributed execution spanning edge devices, local clusters, and clouds.
research_trajectory: From peer-to-peer systems (Chord) and cloud data processing (Spark, Mesos) to serverless systems, Ray distributed AI, and multi-cloud/edge Sky Computing.
funding_projects: Berkeley Sky Industry Consortium (Google, Amazon, Microsoft)

recruitment.evidence_text: Recruiting PhD students through UC Berkeley EECS graduate admissions; looking for candidates with strong systems building skills.

potential_phd_topics: Sky Computing: Federated Resource Orchestration Spanning Heterogeneous Edge and Multi-Cloud
Ray-Edge: Lightweight Distributed Actor Runtimes for Resource-Constrained Edge Micro-Clusters
Collaborative Low-Latency Large Language Model Inference Across the Edge-Cloud Boundary
why_suitable: Legendary systems researcher responsible for transformative systems (Spark, Ray, Chord, Databricks)
Co-leads Berkeley Sky Computing Lab, the epicenter of modern cloud-edge and distributed AI research
Fully funded 5-year GRA fellowship package at UC Berkeley EECS
Unrivalled industrial network and impact on production distributed architectures
research_gaps: Actor state persistence overhead in Ray when nodes at the network edge face sudden power failure
Cost-latency optimization for multi-cloud inter-region and edge egress bandwidth

publications.title: From cloud computing to sky computing
publications.venue: Proceedings of the Workshop on Hot Topics in Operating Systems
publications.research_problem: Cloud computing is fragmented across providers instead of acting as a coherent utility.
publications.approach: Position paper envisioning 'sky computing' and arguing the barriers are more economic than technical.
publications.key_contribution: Proposes reciprocal peering between clouds as the key enabling step toward sky computing.
publications.edge_relevance: Cloud Computing and Resource Management (Information Systems)

research_trajectory: From convex optimization for communication networks to Fog computing, edge network slicing, and telecommunications economics.

Pioneer in mathematical optimization, network utility maximization, and edge resource economics

research_trajectory: From distributed graph analytics (GraphLab) to machine learning systems, video analytics pipelines, and LLM serving runtimes (vLLM).

Direct research in model serving efficiency, memory management, and edge inference

publications.title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
publications.research_problem: Severe DRAM memory fragmentation in KV cache limits concurrent throughput during model serving.

publications.key_contribution: Increases serving throughput by 2-4x without altering model accuracy.
publications.edge_relevance: Crucial technique for deploying large models on resource-constrained edge memory.

publications.title: A Lyapunov Theory for Finite-Sample Guarantees of Markovian Stochastic Approximation
publications.research_problem: Stochastic approximation underpins large-scale optimisation and reinforcement learning, but its finite-sample behaviour under Markovian noise lacked a unified analysis.
publications.approach: A Lyapunov framework built on a smooth generalised Moreau envelope for contractive operators under arbitrary norms.
publications.key_contribution: Finite-sample guarantees applied to TD-learning variants and Q-learning, with insight into bootstrapping and eligibility traces.

publications.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Interactive Mobile Wearable and Ubiquitous Technologies
publications.research_problem: Smart-home routines that access the same devices at the same time conflict, and it is unclear which resolution strategies users prefer.
